messages:
maya: Quick proposal — want to try a 'catalog risk budget' for Q2 to let us onboard more experimental models while limiting churn. Idea: short-lived onboards (14d TTL) + hard metric gates. keeps customers safe and lets product iterate faster. thoughts?

liam: sounds promising. can you sketch the budget math? what's the limit per quarter and how do we measure 'churn'?

maya: plan sketch: each model gets a risk score (low/med/high). we allocate a fixed number of high-risk onboards per quarter (e.g., 6), medium (12), unlimited low. high-risk requires 2 customer opt-ins + SRE canary. TTL enforced so if it fails we auto-retire. churn measured as percent of customer-facing model swaps that are rollbacks or deprecations within 30d. goal: keep churn <= 3%/quarter.

anna: need concrete gates. what are the acceptance metrics for an experimental model to graduate from TTL to permanent?

maya: graduate if: 1) benchmark pass on our core eval suite (delta vs baseline): p95 latency no more than +20ms, cost per token delta < 15%, and quality regressions < 2% on prompt sets. 2) 2 weeks without customer-facing rollbacks. 3) runbook + owner assigned.

oliver: also add an automatic fallback policy: if user requests a pinned variant and the new model breaches quality/cost thresholds, route back to pinned model for that tenant. avoids customer-visible errors.

carter: implementation question — how do we tag TTL models in the catalog? prefer metadata flags so Console/SDK can show 'experimental, expires: <date>'.

maya: agreed. propose CLI / API flags, e.g.:

```
rb model create --name "orca-test" --risk=high --fast-ttl=14d --owner=@anna
```

and the catalog UI shows a countdown + expiry actions (migrate/pin/auto-retire).

devops-bot: Scheduled canary job created: canary/orca-test every 12h. Logs -> https://ci.redwood.example/canaries/1744444444

liam: one big risk is internal operational load from many short TTLs. can we add a 'risk credit' chargeback to teams creating high-risk onboards? slows spammy experimenting.

maya: yes — risk credits idea: product teams have quarterly budget. creating high-risk consumes 2 credits, medium 1. credits replenish next quarter or can be requested with a short justification. tracks ownership.

anna: on the customer side, we need an opt-in button and clear comms: "This model is experimental and may be retired after 14 days; we'll notify you and suggest migrations." Also a checkbox to auto-fallback to previous pinned model.

oliver: engineering notes: telemetry we need per-tenant: p95 latency, tokens-per-request, hallucination proxy (eval prompts), and rollback trigger counts. store with model_version tag so we can backfill. estimate ~1.5GB/day extra metrics for 100 onboards.

carter: can support team handle escalation? propose a one-pager playbook for dev support + SRE for TTL rollbacks. also SLA for owner to respond within 24h for any regression alerts.

maya: action items: 1) eng (oliver/carther) to prototype TTL tag + auto-retire UI and CLI, 2) infra (liam) to calculate budget simulation and risk credits, 3) product (maya/anna) to draft customer opt-in copy + playbook. sync in 3 days.

liam: +1. i'll run a simulation and share numbers tomorrow.

anna: i'll draft the acceptance gate checks and the email/web copy for opt-ins.

maya: thanks — if we can get this shipped as an 'experimental lane' it should unblock several internal pilots that are stuck waiting for a permanent pin. :rocket:
